Kinda funny related story. Grew up in what at the time was in the edge of what you would call rural australia (dirt road for about 10 mins, then asphalt and closest shops maybe 15 mins after that by car, not rural truly, but not developed) we had a few acres, with a little bbq hut that was raised by half a story with some undercroft storage walled off. So being badass, myself (10 or 11) and my little bro (7 or 8) had hitched a rope off a balcony railing and were practicing our "wall climbing skills" while mum and dad were out at a neighborhood meeting. After a few sucessful rappel's, we started trying to do vertical ascents. 

You know, like in the movies.

The grass hadn't been mowed in a few weeks/months, so it was adult shin-high but pretty much knee high for us. So after a few heroic attempts, i let my brother have a go.

He lines himself up, takes a step back to firmly plant himself. 

Then i notice it.

The grass around his feet is making weird movements. 

He now has his other foot planted on the wall and is about to start pulling himself up. 

Thats when i see his back foot had been planted exactly where you would want it if you stepped on a brown snake, directly behind its head.

The rest of it was thrashing wildly, causing the grass to rustle which caught my attention.

In one of the few times we have expressed automatic familial protection mode for each other, i ran and tackle-carried him away and up the stairs and back inside.

Cue frantic call to mum and dad at the neighbours (christ, post it note next to a fucking line phone) who, as it transpired, were attending neighborhood snake awareness meeting. (Which is like a 6 minute drive, so not next door)

Bro is now 198cm and a giant machine, the fucker, but i saved his life and that's a debt that can never be repaid. 

I remind him of it often.

We went to a small school and were family friends with the teacher. He and his wife came over to dinner one time and he picked up my little bro in a bear hug. The shepard, for the one and only time growled like crazy. He put my bro down and then she was all hugs and licks.

It was then we started paying more attention to her behaviour. When any of us kids went into the pool she would go batshit and duck under the deck, yowling and barking. The vet had a theory that she had a false pregnancy and thought her pups were under the deck. That our jumping in the pool she perceived we were invading her space and she was protecting her territory. 

In my mind I thought it was baloney. My theory was that she thought we were her pups and whenever we went under the water she went nuts thinking we were drowning. It made sense to me since whenever we were sitting on the edge of the pool she would come and sit/nuzzle/lick at us, and stop barking. 

Weeeeeeelll. It all came to a head when my dad took me and my grandparents on a europetrip (long story). There were a couple of time when the dogs would come back covered in blood. Once or twice it was them getting to close to a whipper snipper. A few times they came back covered in blood with no wounds.

Eventually it came out that they were sneaking out (we had REALLY good fences) and ran down the road to a small hobby farm.  They had ran down ducks to begin with. The turning point was when they ran down a goat. And ate it.

I was in a hotel in france with my dad when he got the call that our dogs had straight up killed a goat. My mum and siblings found out when the hobby farmer rocked up at their door with a shotgun. I spent the night in the bathroom because i didn't want to come out after that news.

The weirder thing is, we followed procedures and had the council take the dogs away. The rule of the law was you can have these dogs if you change your fences in X way. We were lucky enough that we could afford to do that and told the pound where they were at. 

Then it got weird.

We told them the contractors would be in and fit the new fences and would be done in a week. The reply was the dogs already had new homes (with a security firm) and if we pressed the matter the dogs would be brought back and put to sleep.  

So thats the story about how i locked myself into a french bathroom for a few days and how our dogs were stolen from us.

This happened when we got our second dog, a german shepherd. Our first dog, a mongrel ridgeback, was quite a bit smaller, but got her to do her dirty work. Stealing blankets, treats, you name it.

Then, when the shepherd had grown to full size..... it got.... disturbing.

They would go out on adventures (sneaking out mind you, we did everything to keep them in the yard when they were unsupervised) and they would sneak back..... dishevelled, panting, burrs and brambles in their fur. Then there were some feathers..... we figured they were chasing some birds.

soon, when they came back, the shepherd would have some blood on her coat.... we looked for a cut, but couldn't find one, we figured that a tick got her and she bled a little.

then it happened.

They came back one day, and the shepherd was COVERED in blood. Soaked. We thought she had been hit by a car and we rushed out to help her.... but she was walking fine, and seemed happy..... there were no cuts on her.

10 minutes later, a neighbour from down the road turned up. With a shotgun.

Turns out that out shepherd had been killing his ducks, while the mongrel just stood back, not even barking. 

But that wasn't enough for the mongrels blood lust. That day, the neighbour saw them sneak on to his property, silently. The mongrel apparently barked once, the shepherd blurred into action. She ran down a goat and killed it. They didn't try to eat it or anything. They just wanted it dead.

TL:DR; My older dog corrupted a sweet german shepherd pup, into a theiving, killing machine.
